summary: Interactive 3D brass butterfly with exploded parts view, flight controls, and spec sheet generated in Three.js.

post.originalText:
One prompt built this: a brass butterfly that takes itself apart, gear by gear.

A hidden Google model, reportedly Gemini 4 Pro, one-shotted it in three.js.

Then the model disappeared.

The request was simple: make a beautiful mechanical butterfly. No follow-ups. The arena only allows one message per matchup, so this is a single try.

What came back wasn't just a 3D model. It was a full interactive page.

→ a slider that explodes the butterfly into its parts
→ every part labeled, from the wing actuator to the nine-ring abdomen
→ two themes, gold with azure glass or black steel
→ a "take flight" button, orbit camera, four views

Watch it come apart at 0:08.

It also wrote itself a spec sheet. 6.2 m wingspan, 2.4 kg, wings beating 2.3 times a second.

Nobody asked for a spec sheet. It wrote one anyway.

Here's the catch. It was running under a fake name, "gemini-3.7-flash." By the next morning it was gone from the arena, and more than 60 retries got nothing back.

To be clear: Google hasn't confirmed which model this is. It's one output, not a benchmark, and Gemini has always been strong at 3D front-end work.

But if one prompt gets you this, a lot of paid landing-page work just got a lot harder to sell.

Unreleased Gemini 4 Pro, or a Flash model hiding under a fake name?
